judged_text: The refresh_token placeholder fallback mutates and returns a credential-shaped object for non-sync paths too, where callers like Zoom expect the full parsed schema and now get a possibly mutated object. In zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts the result of parseRefreshTokenResponse is used instead of the previous zoomRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse; if the Zoom response legitimately contains refresh_token (Zoom rotates refresh tokens), the placeholder logic is a no-op, but any caller whose real schema treats refresh_token as required can no longer distinguish a genuinely missing refresh_token from the injected placeholder, and the stored credential is updated with the fake value 'refresh_token' as if it were a real token — a credential-corruption write that downstream refresh flows will use verbatim.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful parse the code unconditionally injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { ... }`). This behavior is not limited to the sync/minimum-schema branch; it occurs for any successful parse where `refresh_token` is absent/optional. Call sites were changed to use this helper (e.g. `packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)`), which can mask a genuinely missing/omitted `refresh_token` and can propagate a fake refresh token value downstream (and potentially into persisted credentials, depending on the caller’s update logic).
